note: Thu vien dung chung: the y (cards), tu dien cum (phraseBank), tu thay the (upgrades). Slot: {act} = cum danh dong (gerund) lam chu ngu, {who} = nhom nguoi (so nhieu), {problem} = cum danh tu van de. {field} = linh vuc (mac dinh education).

P1.label: Kỹ năng việc làm và kinh tế
P1.short: stronger job prospects and economic growth
P1.pred: builds the job-ready skills that employers look for
s: {act} equips {who} with the competencies that modern employers actively seek.
Today's labour market rewards individuals who combine solid knowledge with adaptability and initiative, and such an approach nurtures precisely these qualities.
As a result, graduates are better placed to secure stable, well-paid employment, which in turn boosts productivity and drives long-term economic growth.
Employers also spend less on retraining new recruits, which makes the country a more attractive destination for investment.
P1.ex: A case in point is South Korea, whose sustained investment in schooling underpinned its rise to a high-income economy.

P2.label: Cơ hội bình đẳng, thăng tiến xã hội
P2.pred: narrows the gap between rich and poor
s: {act} plays a pivotal role in levelling the playing field between wealthy and disadvantaged families.
Without adequate public support, quality learning tends to become a privilege reserved for those who can afford it, leaving talented children from poorer backgrounds with limited prospects.
When opportunities are widely accessible, young people can progress on merit rather than family wealth, which narrows the social divide and strengthens social mobility.
In this way, talent is discovered wherever it exists, instead of being wasted through lack of funds.
P2.ex: Finland's free, publicly funded system, which delivers consistently strong results regardless of family income, illustrates this effect.

P3.label: Phát triển toàn diện, sức khỏe tinh thần
s: {act} contributes to the all-round development of {who}, not merely their academic results.
Experiences of this kind nurture creativity, self-confidence and emotional resilience, qualities that conventional lessons often neglect.
Learners who feel motivated and mentally balanced tend to concentrate better and perform more consistently across the curriculum.
Schools that value this wider growth therefore produce graduates who are healthier in mind as well as stronger in exams.
P3.ex: For instance, a pupil who gains confidence by performing in a school concert is likely to speak up more readily in other lessons.

P4.label: Giá trị xã hội, làm việc nhóm
P4.pred: fosters responsibility and respect for others
s: {act} fosters social and moral values that classroom lessons alone rarely instil.
Through teamwork, shared responsibility and contact with peers who hold different viewpoints, {who} learn to cooperate, show tolerance and respect rules.
These habits carry over into adult life, producing citizens who are more considerate and more willing to contribute to their communities.
Such an environment also lowers the risk of bullying and exclusion, because pupils learn early to value one another.
P4.ex: For example, pupils who complete a group project learn to negotiate disagreements rather than avoid them.

P5.label: Tư duy phản biện, hiểu sâu
s: {act} encourages {who} to think analytically instead of merely memorising facts.
When learners are expected to question, compare and justify their ideas, they grasp concepts more thoroughly and retain them for far longer.
This capacity for independent reasoning is invaluable at university and in the workplace, where problems rarely come with a ready-made answer.
Employers and universities alike prize graduates who can evaluate evidence critically instead of simply repeating it.
P5.ex: A student who has debated a social issue in class, for instance, will find it easier to construct a coherent argument in an essay or a meeting.

P6.label: Linh hoạt, dễ tiếp cận (công nghệ/online)
P6.pred: makes study flexible and widely accessible
s: {act} makes learning considerably more flexible and accessible.
With a laptop and an internet connection, {who} are able to attend lessons from remote areas, revisit recorded explanations and study at times that suit their personal circumstances.
This convenience widens participation, particularly among working adults, rural residents and people with health conditions who might otherwise be excluded.
At the same time, institutions are able to serve far larger cohorts without constructing additional buildings.
P6.ex: Platforms such as Coursera and Khan Academy, for example, now offer university-level material to millions of users free of charge.

P7.label: Cá nhân hóa việc học
s: {act} allows teaching to be tailored to the needs of each individual learner.
In a crowded classroom, a teacher rarely has time to adjust the pace for every child, whereas adaptive software or one-to-one guidance can pinpoint weaknesses and offer targeted practice.
Consequently, struggling students receive timely support while quicker learners are stretched, so overall progress becomes noticeably more even.
Teachers, freed from repetitive marking, are then able to devote more attention to discussion and encouragement.
P7.ex: A pupil who repeatedly makes the same grammar mistake, for instance, receives tailored exercises the same day instead of waiting weeks for feedback.

P8.label: Tầm nhìn toàn cầu, ngôn ngữ, văn hóa
P8.pred: opens doors in a globalised job market
s: {act} broadens the horizons of {who} and prepares them for an increasingly interconnected world.
Exposure to other languages and cultures builds communication skills and open-mindedness, both of which multinational employers value highly.
It also weakens prejudice, since people who understand different traditions are less likely to rely on stereotypes.
In the long run, such connections between nations also strengthen trade, tourism and diplomatic goodwill.
P8.ex: For example, a graduate who is fluent in two languages may apply for roles in several countries, which multiplies their career options.

P9.label: Lợi ích xã hội (sức khỏe, tội phạm)
P9.short: wider benefits for health and public safety
P9.pred: brings wider benefits for public health and community safety
s: Beyond personal advancement, {act} brings wider benefits to society as a whole.
Educated individuals are statistically more inclined to make healthier lifestyle choices and less prone to criminal behaviour.
This ultimately yields safer communities and eases the burden on healthcare and law enforcement, freeing public money for other priorities.
Society therefore recoups a sizeable part of what it spends, often many times over.
P9.ex: A community in which most residents have completed secondary school, for example, typically reports lower crime and healthier habits.

P10.label: Tiết kiệm chi phí
P10.pred: reduces costs for learners and providers
s: {act} is often considerably cheaper than the traditional alternative.
Learners avoid expenses such as commuting, accommodation and printed textbooks, while institutions save on buildings and staff, so fees can be kept lower.
The same content therefore reaches far more people at a fraction of the price.
Savings of this kind can be redirected towards better materials or extra support for struggling learners.
P10.ex: A university course delivered online, for example, may cost a fraction of its on-campus equivalent.

P11.label: Chuẩn đánh giá khách quan, tạo động lực
P11.pred: gives a clear and objective measure of achievement
s: {act} provides a clear and objective standard of achievement.
Standardised results allow teachers, parents and employers to compare performance fairly, and the prospect of an exam motivates many students to revise systematically.
Without such benchmarks, standards could vary widely from school to school.
Employers and universities can also treat grades as a trustworthy signal of what a candidate has actually mastered.
P11.ex: A national examination, for instance, lets a university compare applicants from different regions on equal terms.

P12.label: An ninh, trật tự công cộng
s: {act} safeguards public safety, which is the foundation of everyday life.
Residents who feel secure are more likely to work, invest and send their children to school, whereas high crime discourages business and drives people away.
Visible, well-resourced policing can therefore deter offences before they occur and shorten emergency response times.
Confidence in public safety, in turn, encourages investment and keeps communities cohesive.
P12.ex: A neighbourhood with regular patrols, for instance, tends to experience fewer break-ins.

C1.label: Chi phí công, chi phí cơ hội
s: {act} would demand considerable public funds, and these are never unlimited.
Governments must also finance hospitals, transport and social care, so every extra pound committed to one area inevitably leaves less for the others.
Unless the benefits are clearly proven, such spending is difficult to justify and may offer poor value for taxpayers.
Poorer regions, which can least afford such expenditure, would be the first to feel the strain.
C1.ex: A new national programme, for instance, can cost millions before a single pupil sees any improvement.

C2.label: Chương trình quá tải, thiếu thời gian
s: {act} risks overloading a timetable that is already full.
Schools have only a limited number of hours each week, so adding new demands inevitably reduces the time available for core subjects such as literacy, mathematics and science.
As a result, pupils may end up with a superficial understanding of many topics instead of a solid grasp of the essentials.
Teachers would also face pressure to cover more material without any extension of lesson time.
C2.ex: A teacher who must squeeze one more compulsory unit into the term, for example, will have to hurry through material that students find difficult.

C3.label: Áp lực, căng thẳng, kiệt sức
s: {act} tends to place {who} under excessive and prolonged pressure.
Constant deadlines, comparison with classmates and fear of failure often lead to anxiety, sleepless nights and, in severe cases, burnout.
Under such strain, learners gradually lose their curiosity and motivation, which undermines the very results the system is trying to achieve.
Left unchecked, chronic stress may even damage physical and mental health well beyond the school years.
C3.ex: South Korea, where competition for exam results is intense, has long struggled with high stress levels among its teenagers.

C4.label: Xao nhãng, thiếu tương tác trực tiếp
C4.pred: invites distraction and weakens human contact
s: {act} carries the danger of distraction and reduced human contact.

Devices offer endless temptations such as games and social media, and learners who study alone on a screen miss the encouragement, discipline and immediate feedback that a face-to-face teacher provides.
Over time, this may weaken concentration as well as communication skills, both of which are essential for study and work.
Teachers, meanwhile, spend valuable lesson time managing devices instead of explaining ideas.
C4.ex: A student who is supposed to be watching an online lecture, for instance, may find it all too easy to switch to a video platform instead.

C5.label: Khoảng cách số, bất bình đẳng
s: {act} may deepen existing inequalities.
Not every family can afford a modern device or a reliable internet connection, so children from low-income or rural households are likely to fall further behind.
Instead of narrowing the gap, such reliance on technology risks creating a two-tier system in which advantage is determined by wealth.
The very pupils who most need support are therefore the ones least likely to receive it.
C5.ex: During school closures, for example, many pupils without a laptop at home struggled to follow lessons at all.

C6.label: Trách nhiệm của gia đình, nhà nước can thiệp
C6.pred: intrudes on matters that belong to the family
s: {act} intrudes on matters that arguably belong to the family.
Parents are best placed to pass on their own values, beliefs and financial habits, and these differ widely between households.
When the state steps in, it may clash with parental wishes and weaken the sense of personal accountability that young people need to develop.
Public money would be better spent on ensuring that families have the resources to fulfil this role themselves.
C6.ex: A family with strong religious convictions, for instance, may object to a standardised lesson on the subject.

C7.label: Đánh giá hẹp, học vẹt
C7.pred: gives only a narrow picture of ability
s: {act} gives only a narrow picture of ability.
Such assessments mainly reward memory and speed under timed conditions, while creativity, teamwork and practical skills go unmeasured.
Consequently, talented individuals who simply perform poorly in exam halls may be unfairly labelled as weak, and teaching tends to drift towards test preparation.
A fairer picture would combine several forms of evidence gathered over a longer period.
C7.ex: A gifted artist or entrepreneur, for example, may leave school with unimpressive grades despite exceptional real-world potential.

C8.label: Gánh nặng tài chính, cảm xúc cá nhân
C8.pred: places a heavy financial and emotional burden on individuals
s: {act} places a heavy burden on individuals, both financially and emotionally.
Tuition, accommodation and living expenses can consume a family's savings, while unfamiliar surroundings leave some students isolated and struggling.
Consequently, those who cannot cope may finish with debts and disappointing results instead of the advantages they had anticipated.
Such pressure is hard to justify when less costly alternatives are available.
C8.ex: A student who borrows heavily to study overseas, for instance, may spend years repaying the loan.

C9.label: Cô lập xã hội
s: {act} risks leaving {who} socially isolated.
School is where children learn to make friends, resolve disagreements and work in groups, and studying mostly at home limits these everyday interactions.
Without such experience, some may struggle with confidence and teamwork later in life.
Parents who teach at home, however dedicated, can seldom replicate the diversity of a school community.
C9.ex: A child taught entirely at home, for instance, may find a first job interview or group project unusually daunting.

C10.label: Thiếu chuyên môn, cơ sở vật chất
C10.pred: cannot match the expertise and facilities of schools
s: {act} cannot match the expertise and facilities that schools provide.
Few parents are qualified to teach every subject to a high standard, and laboratories, sports grounds and specialist equipment are rarely available at home.
As a result, pupils may leave with gaps in their knowledge that are difficult to repair later.
Few families can afford the private tutors needed to fill every gap.
C10.ex: A parent with no scientific background, for example, may struggle to guide a teenager through chemistry experiments.

C12.label: Gánh nặng cho giáo viên
s: {act} places considerable demands on teachers.
Staff must prepare materials in several languages, hold advanced language qualifications and adapt lessons for pupils at very different levels, all within the same working day.
Without extra training and support, this additional workload leaves many teachers exhausted and weakens the quality of lessons.
Over time, this pressure contributes to high staff turnover and a shortage of experienced instructors.
C12.ex: A science teacher required to deliver chemistry in a second language, for example, must first master the specialist vocabulary herself.

K1.label: Thiếu ngân sách
s: Chronic underfunding is a major contributor to {problem}.
When budgets are tight, schools cannot recruit enough qualified staff, maintain their buildings or purchase up-to-date materials.
The resulting strain on existing resources makes the situation steadily worse.
Ultimately, it is pupils from the poorest areas who suffer most from this neglect.

K2.label: Quá tải công việc, lương thấp
s: Heavy workloads combined with modest pay are a significant source of {problem}.
Teachers who face long hours, endless paperwork and relatively low salaries often feel undervalued and exhausted, and many either leave the profession or never enter it.
This vicious circle leaves the remaining staff with even more to handle.
Recruitment becomes harder year by year, and standards inevitably slip.

K3.label: Hoàn cảnh kinh tế, xã hội khó khăn
s: Social and economic disadvantage lies behind {problem} in many communities.
Children from low-income households often lack a quiet place to study, adequate nutrition or parental support, which holds back their attainment from an early age.
Without outside assistance, these gaps tend to widen as the years pass.
Such inequality at the starting line is extremely difficult to correct later.

K4.label: Rào cản tài chính (học phí, chi phí sống)
s: Financial barriers play a substantial part in {problem}.
Rising tuition fees, living costs and the loss of income while studying discourage many people from continuing their education or push them into heavy borrowing.
This is particularly true for those from modest backgrounds.
As a result, talented people are lost to education simply because they cannot afford it.

K5.label: Thiếu nhận thức, động lực, định kiến
s: Low awareness and motivation contribute to {problem}.
Where people see little connection between study and tangible rewards, or are held back by stereotypes and busy schedules, they simply do not engage.
Women in technical fields and working adults with family commitments are typical examples.
Unless attitudes shift, even generous provision will go unused.

K6.label: Áp lực học tập, cạnh tranh
s: Intense academic pressure is a leading cause of {problem}.
Heavy workloads, frequent deadlines and competition for good grades leave little time for rest, and students fear that poor results will damage their career prospects.
The constant strain accumulates over months and eventually affects both health and performance.
In the worst cases, it drives students to abandon their courses altogether.

K7.label: Dân số tăng, di cư đô thị
s: Rapid population growth and urban migration contribute to {problem}.
When families move to cities faster than new schools are built, existing classrooms must absorb additional children.
Over time, this pushes class sizes well beyond a manageable level.
The quality of teaching inevitably suffers when each pupil receives less individual attention.

S1.label: Tăng đầu tư, xây dựng
s: Governments should commit more funding to {field}, since this tackles the problem at its source.
Extra money can be channelled into recruiting teachers, constructing classrooms and modernising equipment, which relieves pressure where it is felt most.
Over time, such investment pays for itself through a better-educated and more productive workforce.
Public confidence in the system is likely to rise as visible improvements follow.

S2.label: Ưu đãi, đào tạo, lộ trình nghề nghiệp
s: Authorities should offer attractive incentives such as higher salaries, scholarships and structured career pathways.
Such measures encourage talented individuals to enter and remain in the field, and ongoing training keeps them confident in their roles.
A stable, motivated workforce in turn raises standards for everyone.
Retention improves as well, because satisfied professionals are less inclined to leave.

S3.label: Linh hoạt, chi phí thấp, hỗ trợ tài chính
s: Provision should be made more flexible and affordable.
Subsidised fees, evening and online courses, and grants towards living costs allow people with limited money or time to participate without sacrificing their income.
Barriers fall as a result, and participation rises among groups that were previously excluded.
Society benefits twice over, from higher qualifications and from the extra tax paid by better-paid workers.

S4.label: Truyền thông, hình mẫu, tiếp xúc sớm
s: Awareness campaigns and visible role models would change attitudes towards the subject.
Media campaigns, mentoring by successful professionals and early exposure through school clubs show young people that study leads to rewarding careers.
Once these links become clear, motivation tends to follow.
Over a generation, such campaigns can shift the national mindset more effectively than regulation.

S5.label: Hỗ trợ tâm lý, giảm tải
s: Stronger support systems would reduce the strain on both learners and staff.
Counselling services, mentoring schemes and reasonable limits on workload ensure that problems are identified early instead of escalating into crises.
Prevention of this kind is far less costly than dealing with the consequences later.
Healthier, better supported people also perform more consistently in their studies and jobs.

C13.label: Gian lận, bắt nạt, lạm dụng thiết bị
C13.short: misuse such as cheating and cyberbullying
C13.pred: invites misuse such as cheating and cyberbullying
s: {act} exposes {who} to misuse, from cheating to cyberbullying.
Phones make it easy to cheat in tests, record classmates without consent or circulate hurtful messages, and teachers cannot monitor every screen at once.
A clear ban removes these temptations and gives schools a simple, enforceable rule.
Maintaining discipline in such an environment consumes energy that should be spent on teaching.
C13.ex: A student who photographs a test paper and shares it with friends, for example, undermines fairness for everyone.

S6.label: Phối hợp trường - gia đình - cộng đồng
S6.short: closer cooperation between schools and families
s: Closer cooperation between schools, families and local organisations would reinforce these efforts.
Parents who model good habits at home, teachers who reinforce them in class and community groups that offer activities outside school together create a consistent environment.
When all three pull in the same direction, change becomes lasting rather than temporary.
Responsibility is then shared instead of falling on a single institution.
